answer: Graduated trust makes sybil attacks slow and costly. A new identity starts in the system's kernel with tiny weight, allowed only small, low-risk jobs. Like a grove grown season by season, its weight rises only after peers attest useful work over time, and drops sharply after one bad job. A fake cannot simply mint a jade badge of credibility; the attacker must repeat weeks of auditable labour for every fake, so thousands of convincing identities cost far more time and effort than they can earn.
